hook.line: After any trip, party or long dinner, someone will ask how it went. In Colombia you answer with a tiny *la* that doesn't stand for anything.
hook.es: La pasamos buenísimo en el matrimonio de mi prima.
hook.en: We had a fantastic time at my cousin's wedding.

examples.en: Did you have a good time in Cartagena? (to a friend)
How was the party for you all?

examples.es: Me reí mucho, pero la pasé fatal.
examples.en: I laughed a lot, but I had an awful time.
Have a good time. (to a friend)

rule:
To say how a whole experience went, use *la* + *pasar* + how:
*la pasé bien*, *la pasamos genial*, *la pasaron fatal*.

The *la* doesn't point to anything; it's just part of the phrase, and it never changes. Only *pasar* changes for the person.

English says had a good time. Don't translate that word for word: *tuve un buen tiempo* sounds like a weather report.

It judges the whole thing, not one moment. You can laugh a lot and still *la pasé fatal*.

In Spain you'll hear *lo pasé bien*; in Colombia it's *la*.

options: Did you have a good time?
Did she have a good time?

readAndPick.es: Hernando la pasó genial en la cena.
options: Hernando had a great time at dinner.

readAndPick.es: Vale la pasó mal en el bus.
options: Vale had a bad time on the bus.
Vale had a good time on the bus.
How did she spend the party?

readAndPick.es: Me reí mucho, pero la pasé fatal.
options: I laughed a lot and had a great time.
I laughed a lot, but I had an awful time.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *La pasé* or *Pasé* and type the whole sentence (I had a great time): ___ genial.
yourTurn.why: The phrase needs its little *la*: *la pasé*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: We had an awful time.
Type in Spanish, to a friend: Did you have a good time in Cartagena?
yourTurn.why: To a friend, *pasaste*; the *la* is the same for everyone.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Hernando had a great time at dinner.
yourTurn.answer: Hernando la pasó genial en la cena.
accept: Hernando la pasó muy bien en la cena.
Hernando la pasó buenísimo en la cena.
yourTurn.why: *La* goes right before the verb: *la pasó*.

yourTurn.prompt: Ask the whole group: How was the party for you all?
yourTurn.why: You all is *pasaron*, with *cómo* to ask how.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it about we: *La pasé muy bien.*
Turn it around: *La pasamos genial.* (it was awful)

pitfalls.wrong: Tuve un buen tiempo en la fiesta.
pitfalls.right: La pasé bien en la fiesta.
pitfalls.why: Had a good time doesn't translate word for word; Spanish says *la pasé bien*.

pitfalls.right: La pasé genial en la cena.
pitfalls.why: Almost. The phrase always keeps its *la*.
The *la* never changes, even when it's a group.

personal: Think of your last party, trip or long dinner. How was it? *La pasé…* and where.
